_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::input_format#12. The guidance survives, its stated number does not. The same 12x12x12 cantilever (2197 nodes, 1728 HEX8) is written both ways: inline it is 4306 lines of YAML, via ExodusII it is 388 lines plus one meshio-written .e (eb_prop1 patched to 1). Both exit 0, both pass the same pinned dispy 1.38646642128815859e-04 at TOLERANCE 1e-12, and 4C confirms it read the file mesh ('cell-block 1 (): 1728 cells of type hex8'), so the two routes are interchangeable and the reason to prefer the mesh file is that the deck shrinks by more than a factor of ten. The claim that a >1000-line inline deck 'takes 30+ seconds to parse' did not reproduce: on this run 4C's own INPUT phase was 1.180e-01 s inline against 1.080e-01 s for the ExodusII route — same order, both far under a second. Those figures are printed for the reader and deliberately NOT asserted, because elapsed time is a property of the machine; the verdict rests on the deck sizes, the exit codes and the agreement of the two answers. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: shrink the mesh out of the regime the claim is about: a 2x2x2 cantilever is no longer a >1000-line inline deck and no longer reproduces the pinned answer, so INLINE_DECK_LINES / MESH_NODES / INLINE_OVER_1000_LINES all change and the fixture must go red.
_mutation.to: N = 2                       # far below the regime the claim describes

_mutation.note: break the equivalence of the two routes: point the ExodusII deck at the block id meshio wrote rather than the patched one, so the file-mesh arm no longer reproduces the inline answer and the fixture must go red.
